trophies.guide: Overview: This is the platinum itself, so it is never earned directly — it pops the moment the other 54 trophies are all yours. Treat it as the finish line and plan backwards from it. Steps: 1) Clear the story spine first so every area, activity and strand is unlocked. 2) Do the Chapter 1 balcony meditation for the one missable trophy before you leave Chapter 1. 3) Work the world trophies — stunts, scans, races, robberies — while travelling, not in one late grind. 4) Finish with the 100% checklist and the last Challenges. Tip: PowerPyx rates the platinum 4/10 at roughly 200 hours, all single-player, one playthrough — the only real enemy is leaving the grinds until the end.
trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.source: Official PlayStation trophy list; PowerPyx trophy guide
trophies.trigger: Unlock every other trophy; no multiplayer or DLC needed.

trophies.guide: Overview: Reach 100% on the completion checklist that appears under Progress > Stats after the story ends. It is the longest trophy in the game, but it asks for far less than everything: most side quests are not required and collectibles only count in part. Steps: 1) Finish the story, then open the checklist and screenshot it — that screen, not guesswork, is your task list. 2) Clear the required blocks: every robbery, underwater discovery, shooting range, drone race and Bret quest. 3) Only 70 of the 80 Challenges are needed, so skip the ones that frustrate you. 4) Top up the partial collectible counts last. Tip: Anything you did before the ending already counts, so a thorough first playthrough can leave this at well over half done.
trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.source: Official PlayStation trophy list; PowerPyx trophy guide
trophies.trigger: Finish the 100% Completion checklist (appears after the story under Progress > Stats).

trophies.guide: Overview: Finish the final story mission and close out the campaign. It cannot be missed and needs no special preparation — it is the natural end of the story spine. Steps: 1) Play the chapters in order; the finale only opens after Chapter 5's missions. 2) Before the point-of-no-return feel of the last missions, finish the Chapter 1 meditation if you somehow have a pre-Chapter-2 save — otherwise nothing else is lost by finishing. 3) Complete the final mission and let the credits roll. Tip: Finishing the story first is the right order anyway — the 100% checklist only appears afterwards, and post-story free roam is where the cleanup happens.
trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
trophies.source: Official PlayStation trophy list; PowerPyx trophy guide
trophies.trigger: Finish the final mission.

trophies.guide: Overview: Complete any 250 of the 397 stunts scattered across Leonida — stunt jumps, under-bridge flights, Knife Flights and base jumps all share one counter, so you can favour whichever type suits you. Steps: 1) From the start of the game, attempt every marked jump you drive past; early opportunism is worth dozens of stunts. 2) Keep a fast, durable car and a plane in regular use so jumps and bridge flights are always an option. 3) When you settle in for cleanup, work region by region and use the in-game tracking to see what a region still holds. 4) Save the base jumps for last if heights slow you down — there are more than enough of the other three types. Tip: Failed jumps cost nothing but time, so attempt first and route later.
trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.source: PowerPyx trophy guide; GamesRadar+ trophy list
trophies.trigger: Complete any 250 of the 397 stunts: jumps, under-bridge flights, Knife Flights, base jumps.

trophies.guide: Overview: Scan 100 locations with the WAiNK app — landmarks, curiosities and sculptures all count, and there are far more than 100 in the world. Steps: 1) Make opening WAiNK a habit whenever you arrive somewhere new; the app highlights what nearby can be scanned. 2) Scan on foot during missions and strands rather than making dedicated trips. 3) Dense, built-up areas are the richest hunting — a single Vice City block can hold several scans. 4) Check your count in the Progress menu every few hours so this never becomes an endgame surprise. Tip: The same scan habit feeds Whip It Good, since scanning a vehicle also discovers it — one habit, two trophies.
trophies.name: You WAiNKer!
trophies.source: PowerPyx trophy guide; GamesRadar+ trophy list
trophies.trigger: Scan 100 spots with the WAiNK app: landmarks, curiosities, sculptures.

trophies.guide: Overview: Complete any 3 of the 18 Collectible Card sets. A set only counts when every card in it is found, so depth beats breadth — three finished sets, not eighteen half-finished ones. Steps: 1) Early on, pick the three sets whose cards cluster in areas you visit often. 2) Commit to one set at a time and sweep its locations in a single route. 3) Check the collection screen after each session to see which set is closest to done, and pivot to it. 4) Finish the third set and the trophy pops immediately. Tip: Cards you grab opportunistically still help — they tell you which sets are already part-done when you choose your three.
trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck
trophies.source: PowerPyx trophy guide; GamesRadar+ trophy list
trophies.trigger: Complete 3 Collectible Card sets (there are 18).

trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Overview: Earn gold in all 42 challenges across the 12 Shooting Ranges. This is the skill trophy of the set — the score thresholds, not the clock, are the challenge. Steps: 1) Clear each range's challenges once to learn the target patterns before chasing gold. 2) Match the weapon to the challenge: fast-firing for target volume, precise for distance work. 3) Repeat a failed challenge immediately while the pattern is fresh instead of moving on. 4) Work one range to full gold before travelling to the next, so travel never breaks your rhythm. Tip: Accuracy streaks matter more than raw speed on most challenges — slow down one beat and the gold scores get easier, not harder.
trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.source: PowerPyx trophy guide; GamesRadar+ trophy list
trophies.trigger: Gold in all 42 challenges across the 12 Shooting Ranges.

trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Overview: Complete 8 full Strangers & Freaks strands. Individual strand trophies (Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy, Tyrone and Bret's hunts) each count toward this total, so most of the eight arrive while you chase those. Steps: 1) Accept every stranger introduction the story puts in front of you — strands unlock chapter by chapter. 2) Finish strands rather than starting them all; only a completed strand counts. 3) If you reach the late game short of eight, revisit earlier strangers — several open follow-up missions after their first meeting. 4) The eighth completed strand pops the trophy. Tip: The 100% checklist does not require these quests, which is why the roadmap leaves them to the cleanup phase — but their own trophies make them worth finishing regardless.
trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks
trophies.source: PowerPyx trophy guide; GamesRadar+ trophy list
trophies.trigger: Finish 8 Strangers & Freaks questlines.

trophies.guide: Overview: Rob any 5 of the 8 bank vaults and escape afterwards — a robbery only counts when you get away, so the escape plan matters as much as the robbery. Steps: 1) Scout each vault's exits and park a fast getaway vehicle before you go in. 2) Rob the vault, then break line of sight immediately rather than fighting the response. 3) Change vehicles or go to ground until the wanted level clears. 4) Repeat at four more vaults; any five of the eight count. Tip: Robberies are also required on the 100% checklist, so these five are never wasted effort — pick the five vaults nearest your other cleanup routes.
trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal
trophies.source: PowerPyx trophy guide; GamesRadar+ trophy list
trophies.trigger: Rob 5 of the 8 bank vaults and get away.

trophies.guide: Overview: Complete 50 of the 80 Challenges the game tracks across combat, driving, exploration and more. Most players will be most of the way there without trying — this trophy is about deliberately finishing the close ones. Steps: 1) Open the Challenges list after the story and sort by progress. 2) Bank every challenge sitting at 80% or better first; that alone is often a dozen completions. 3) Pick the next targets from categories you enjoy, since only 50 of 80 are needed. 4) Leave the handful of notorious challenges alone entirely — the maths lets you. Tip: The 100% checklist wants 70 Challenges, so if you are going for A Long Road anyway, push past 50 and let this pop on the way.
trophies.name: One Last Thing
trophies.source: PowerPyx trophy guide; GamesRadar+ trophy list
trophies.trigger: Complete 50 of the 80 Challenges.

trophies.guide: Overview: Discover 100 different vehicles — and discovering is generous: scanning a vehicle with the WAiNK app counts, so you never need to own or even drive them. Steps: 1) Scan unfamiliar cars whenever you park up or walk a street. 2) Work through car parks, marinas, airfields and wealthy districts, where the vehicle mix changes completely. 3) Boats, bikes and aircraft count too, so scan at docks and hangars, not just roads. 4) The hundredth distinct vehicle pops the trophy. Tip: Pair this with You WAiNKer! — both trophies feed on the same scan-everything habit, and together they take a fraction of the time apart.
trophies.name: Whip It Good
trophies.source: PowerPyx trophy guide; GamesRadar+ trophy list
trophies.trigger: Discover 100 vehicles; a WAiNK scan is enough.

trophies.guide: Overview: Clear the fog from the entire Leonida map by physically visiting every region. There is no trick to it — coverage is what counts. Steps: 1) Explore as you travel between missions instead of fast-travelling over unvisited ground. 2) After the story, open the map and mark the remaining fog patches; they are usually coastlines, islands and the far corners. 3) Take a boat for island fog and a plane for awkward inland pockets. 4) When the last patch clears, the trophy pops. Tip: Exploration overlaps with stunts, scans and meditation spots, so route your fog-clearing through those markers and four counters rise on one trip.
trophies.name: The Goodtime State
trophies.source: PowerPyx trophy guide; GamesRadar+ trophy list
trophies.trigger: Clear the fog from the entire Leonida map.

trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Overview: Meditate at all 18 Meditation Spots — and this is the game's one missable trophy, because one of the meditations is not at a marked spot at all. Steps: 1) In Chapter 1, after one of the early missions, Lucia mentions meditation in the kitchen at Jason's house one morning and heads to the balcony. Follow her, accept the prompt, and meditate with her. The Progress counter rises by 1 even though the balcony is never marked as a Meditation Spot. 2) That moment cannot be repeated after Chapter 1 — if you skip it, the counter can never reach 18 on this save. 3) Meditate at the 17 marked spots at any pace afterwards. 4) The trophy pops at the eighteenth meditation. Tip: Keep a save at the start of Chapter 1 until the balcony meditation is done — it is the only insurance this trophy offers.
trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
trophies.source: PowerPyx trophy guide; GamesRadar+ trophy list
trophies.trigger: Meditate at all 18 Meditation Spots. One meditation — Lucia showing you on the balcony at Jason's house in Chapter 1 — may be required and cannot be repeated after Chapter 1, so do it then.

trophies.guide: Overview: Perform 500 actions that affect your Criminal Profile — the crimes, heists and illicit acts the game quietly tallies as you play. Steps: 1) Simply play the game the way it encourages: robberies, escapes and story choices all move the profile. 2) Check the profile count in the Progress menu from time to time so you know it is climbing. 3) If you reach the endgame short of 500, ordinary free-roam crime — robberies in particular — closes the gap quickly. 4) The five-hundredth counted action pops the trophy. Tip: There is no single action to grind; variety counts the same as repetition, so never farm one act 500 times.
trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder
trophies.source: PowerPyx trophy guide; GamesRadar+ trophy list
trophies.trigger: Perform 500 actions that affect your Criminal Profile.

trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Overview: Try each of the 9 activity types once — fishing, hunting, golf, a shooting range, pool, basketball, a video game, a race and a stunt. Trying is enough; you do not need to win, score or even finish well. Steps: 1) Sample each activity the first time the map offers it, rather than postponing them all. 2) Keep a mental checklist — the nine are easy to lose track of across a 200-hour game. 3) The home TV covers the video game; any race start line covers the race. 4) The ninth distinct activity pops the trophy. Tip: This is the cheapest trophy in the game for its Gamerscore — an afternoon of sampling earns it, and it teaches you the activities their own trophies later demand.
trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.source: PowerPyx trophy guide; GamesRadar+ trophy list
trophies.trigger: Try all 9 activity types: fishing, hunting, golf, shooting range, pool, basketball, a video game, a race, a stunt.

trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Overview: Win a Top Fun drone race at each of the 14 locations — unlike Master of None, a win is required at every single one. Steps: 1) Fly each course once to learn its gates and tight turns before racing for the win. 2) Cut corners on the racing line rather than following the course's visual centre. 3) Retry a lost location immediately; drone races are short and the course knowledge fades fast. 4) Bank wins region by region so your remaining list is always visible at a glance. Tip: Drone races are also on the 100% checklist, so treat the 14 wins as required work, not a side hobby.
trophies.name: Top Fun
trophies.source: PowerPyx trophy guide; GamesRadar+ trophy list
trophies.trigger: Win a Top Fun drone race at each of the 14 locations.

trophies.guide: Overview: Win 20 different races out of the 40 available. Distinct is the key word — winning the same race twenty times counts once. Steps: 1) Enter races as you encounter them across the map and note which ones you have won. 2) Bring a competitive vehicle for the class; an underpowered entry wastes a trip. 3) If a race resists, move on — you only need half the races in the game, so pick the twenty that suit you. 4) The twentieth distinct win pops the trophy. Tip: Mix race types as you travel and the count climbs without a dedicated grind; leave a deliberate mop-up list of five or six unwon races for one evening.
trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
trophies.source: PowerPyx trophy guide; GamesRadar+ trophy list
trophies.trigger: Win 20 different races (out of 40).

trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Overview: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge. Cal's strand starts in Chapter 1, so this is one of the earliest side trophies available. Steps: 1) Meet Cal in Chapter 1 and follow his fishing strand as it opens. 2) Practise the fishing mechanics on ordinary catches before the contest — timing the catch is the whole skill. 3) Enter the challenge when offered and out-fish him. 4) If you lose, retry the contest; it is repeatable. Tip: Start Cal's strand early even if you postpone the contest — an opened strand waits for you, and fishing practice doubles as progress toward trying every activity.
trophies.name: Baited My Tackle
trophies.source: PowerPyx trophy guide; GamesRadar+ trophy list
trophies.trigger: Beat Cal in a fishing contest; his questline starts in Chapter 1.

trophies.guide: Overview: Beat any one of the 4 video games — three of them are on the TV at home, so no travel is needed. Steps: 1) Sit down at the home TV and try all three games briefly. 2) Pick the one whose controls click with you fastest; only one win is required. 3) Learn its scoring or completion condition, then play proper attempts. 4) The first game you beat pops the trophy. Tip: Treat this as a break trophy — it is the easiest palate cleanser in the list after a long robbery or stunt session.
trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
trophies.source: PowerPyx trophy guide; GamesRadar+ trophy list
trophies.trigger: Beat any one of the 4 video games (three are on the TV at home).

trophies.guide: Overview: Have Jason and Lucia at maximum Strength at the same time. The efficient route is training together: at the gym, while one character works out, the other trains automatically, so both stats rise in parallel. Steps: 1) Visit the gym with both characters and start a joint routine. 2) Repeat sessions across the playthrough rather than in one sitting — Strength builds gradually. 3) Watch both Strength stats in the Progress menu; the trophy needs them maxed simultaneously, not one after the other. 4) When the second character reaches max while the first is still there, it pops. Tip: Start gym visits early — a maxed stat left waiting is fine, but a stat started in the endgame turns this into a pure grind.
trophies.name: Personal Best
trophies.source: PowerPyx trophy guide; GamesRadar+ trophy list
trophies.trigger: Max out Strength for Jason and Lucia at the same time. Train together at the gym: while one works out, the other trains automatically.

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Overview: Complete Andy's strand — 5 quests, played as Lucia, opening in Chapter 3. Steps: 1) Reach Chapter 3 and meet Andy as Lucia; the strand will not start for Jason. 2) Work the five quests in order, returning to Andy between story missions. 3) If a quest seems missing, advance the story a little — strand steps often gate on chapter progress. 4) The fifth and final quest pops the trophy on completion. Tip: Andy's strand also counts toward Strangers & Freaks, so finishing it is double progress — prioritise it over strands with no trophy of their own.
trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation
trophies.source: PowerPyx trophy guide; GamesRadar+ trophy list
trophies.trigger: Finish Andy's 5 quests; Lucia only, from Chapter 3.

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Overview: Clear 7 shipwrecks for Kenton, whose strand is available from Chapter 1 — the earliest strand trophy in the game. Steps: 1) Meet Kenton in Chapter 1 and accept the shipwreck work. 2) Travel to each wreck site, dive it and clear what Kenton needs cleared. 3) Work wrecks in coastal clusters to cut sailing time between them. 4) Clearing the seventh wreck completes the strand and pops the trophy. Tip: Underwater discoveries are also required by the 100% checklist, so Kenton's wrecks pull double duty — do them before random diving.
trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident
trophies.source: PowerPyx trophy guide; GamesRadar+ trophy list
trophies.trigger: Clear 7 shipwrecks for Kenton; from Chapter 1.

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Overview: Complete Billy's 5 quests at the Thrillbilly Mudclub, available from Chapter 2. Steps: 1) Head to the Mudclub once Chapter 2 opens and introduce yourself to Billy. 2) Run his five quests in order, returning to the club between them. 3) Bring an off-road-capable vehicle for the trip out — the club lives up to its name. 4) The fifth quest closes the strand and pops the trophy. Tip: Like the other named strands, Billy's counts toward Strangers & Freaks — five quests here is one-eighth of that silver trophy.
trophies.name: The Lone Rider
trophies.source: PowerPyx trophy guide; GamesRadar+ trophy list
trophies.trigger: Finish Billy's 5 quests at the Thrillbilly Mudclub; from Chapter 2.

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Overview: Deliver all 16 cars on Randy's Wish List, from Chapter 3. This is the longest strand trophy — sixteen specific cars, each found and delivered. Steps: 1) Open the Wish List when the strand starts and keep it in mind while free-roaming; listed cars are worth scanning for constantly. 2) Deliver each car in the condition Randy wants — check the list before the run, not after a damaged arrival. 3) Register finds as you go; the delivery habit here is the same one On the Spot rewards. 4) The sixteenth delivery pops the trophy. Tip: Never pass a Wish List car to chase something else — they are the strand's bottleneck, and a missed sighting can mean hours before it appears again.
trophies.name: Supply & Demand
trophies.source: PowerPyx trophy guide; GamesRadar+ trophy list
trophies.trigger: Deliver all 16 cars on Randy's Wish List; from Chapter 3.

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Overview: Complete Tyrone's strand as Jason, from Chapter 3, ending with the labs destroyed and his final quest done. Steps: 1) Meet Tyrone as Jason in Chapter 3 — the strand will not start for Lucia. 2) Follow the strand's quests in order as they unlock. 3) Come armed for the lab work; those missions are the strand's combat peak. 4) Finishing the last quest pops the trophy. Tip: Tyrone's strand counts toward Strangers & Freaks, and its lab missions also feed your Criminal Profile count for Actions Speak Louder.
trophies.name: Spin On This!
trophies.source: PowerPyx trophy guide; GamesRadar+ trophy list
trophies.trigger: Destroy the labs and finish Tyrone's last quest; Jason only, from Chapter 3.

trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Overview: The official description says only this: hunt a unique animal for Bret, playing as Jason. The trigger is unconfirmed — published lists agree the exact animal has not been reliably identified yet, so this guide states plainly what is known and invents no animal, place or method. Steps: 1) Play Bret's strand as Jason and take every hunt it offers. 2) Study animals through your binoculars as you travel, so unique specimens stand out when one appears. 3) When Bret names a target in-game, follow the game's own wording — it is the only confirmed source. Tip: Bret's quests are required on the 100% checklist anyway, so his strand is never wasted time while the community confirms this trigger.
trophies.name: Fair Game
trophies.source: Official PlayStation trophy list; trigger unconfirmed in published lists
trophies.trigger: Hunt a unique animal for Bret; Jason only. The exact animal is still being confirmed.

trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: Overview: Reach a 4-star wanted level with your partner beside you, then lose it completely. The escape, not the crime, is the skill being tested. Steps: 1) Commit crimes together until the wanted level reaches 4 stars — your partner must be with you. 2) Break line of sight and head for cover that blocks the search: the published route is the train tunnel north of Ambrosia in Kelly County, where the police lose track of you. 3) Stay hidden until the heat fully clears; being spotted restarts the escape. 4) The trophy pops once the wanted level is gone. Tip: Set up the tunnel run before you raise the stars — knowing the escape route in advance is the difference between one attempt and five.
trophies.name: Hot Together
trophies.source: PowerPyx trophy guide; GamesRadar+ trophy list
trophies.trigger: Escape a 4-star wanted level together with your partner. Easiest escape: the train tunnel north of Ambrosia in Kelly County.

trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: Overview: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner, keeping a wanted level alive the whole time — lose the heat between shops and the chain resets. Steps: 1) Pick a tight cluster: the three jewelry stores in north Vice City are the published route. 2) Rob the first store with your partner, then move straight to the second without hiding long enough to clear your stars. 3) Rob the second and third the same way, keeping the wanted level ticking over. 4) Leave the third store and wait — the trophy pops about half a minute later. Tip: Park one fast car between the stores before you start; the chain is won or lost on travel time, not on the robberies themselves.
trophies.name: Retail Therapy
trophies.source: PowerPyx trophy guide; GamesRadar+ trophy list
trophies.trigger: Rob 3 shops in a row with your partner while staying wanted. The three jewelry stores in north Vice City work well; the trophy pops about half a minute after you leave the third store.

trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Overview: Rob a jewelry store without being detected at any point. It needs the Snap Gun, which only arrives in Chapter 3, so this cannot be attempted early. Steps: 1) Wait until you have the Snap Gun, then choose a jewelry store and case it — entrances, staff and sightlines. 2) Enter quietly and take the goods without raising an alarm or being spotted. 3) Leave the same way you came in. 4) If you are seen at any point, the attempt is void — walk away and restart clean rather than salvaging it. Tip: Attempt this store fresh, not as the third stop of a Retail Therapy chain — stealth and a live wanted level do not mix.
trophies.name: Sneakthief
trophies.source: PowerPyx trophy guide; GamesRadar+ trophy list
trophies.trigger: Rob a jewelry store undetected (needs the Snap Gun from Chapter 3).

trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Overview: Rob an armored truck and escape. Any truck on its route counts, so the trophy is about picking your moment. Steps: 1) Watch for an armored truck on a quiet stretch of road rather than in dense traffic. 2) Stop the truck, take the cash quickly, and do not linger. 3) Break away immediately and lose the response before it builds. 4) Once you are clear with the money, the trophy pops. Tip: A pre-parked getaway vehicle one block from the hit turns a messy escape into a short one — set it up before you engage the truck.
trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play
trophies.source: PowerPyx trophy guide; GamesRadar+ trophy list
trophies.trigger: Rob an armored truck and get away.

trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Overview: Rob one illegal operation belonging to each of the 9 gangs. With 39 operations in the world, each gang offers you a choice — you need breadth across gangs, not depth in one. Steps: 1) Keep a tally of which gangs you have hit; nine gangs, one operation each. 2) For each gang, pick its easiest operation — the smallest, quietest site you can find. 3) Rob it and escape; the gang is then done, however many operations it has left. 4) The ninth gang's operation pops the trophy. Tip: Gang operations are also ideal Gunslinger targets — clustered enemies in one place — so plan the two trophies together.
trophies.name: Pest Control
trophies.source: PowerPyx trophy guide; GamesRadar+ trophy list
trophies.trigger: Rob one illegal operation from each of the 9 gangs (39 exist).

trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Overview: Take all 3 key valuables from the Kingpin Bowling alley in Port Gellhorn, then lose the police. All three items are required — leaving with two earns nothing. Steps: 1) Go to Kingpin Bowling in Port Gellhorn and locate the 3 key valuables inside. 2) Take all three before making your exit. 3) Leave and lose your wanted level completely. 4) The trophy counts once you are clear of the heat with all three items. Tip: Scout the alley on a quiet visit first, so the robbery itself is a straight line from item to item to exit.
trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling
trophies.source: PowerPyx trophy guide; GamesRadar+ trophy list
trophies.trigger: Take all 3 key valuables from Kingpin Bowling in Port Gellhorn and lose the police.

trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Overview: Launder $250,000 worth of Marked Bills through your fence contacts. Marked bills come from robberies, and fences clean them for a cut — this is a cumulative total, earned in instalments. Steps: 1) Rob regularly; vaults and operations are your supply of marked bills. 2) Visit a fence after every big score instead of stockpiling bills. 3) Keep a rough running total so you know whether you are at $80,000 or $230,000. 4) The laundering that crosses $250,000 pops the trophy. Tip: This is a slow burn by design — players who launder after every score finish it mid-game, while players who ignore fences face a pure grind at the end.
trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar
trophies.source: PowerPyx trophy guide; GamesRadar+ trophy list
trophies.trigger: Launder $250,000 in marked bills through fences.

trophies.guide: Overview: Spend $100,000 across any shops in Leonida — weapons, clothes, vehicles, anything sold counts toward one total. Steps: 1) Spend normally as you gear up; early weapons and vehicles move the counter fastest. 2) Do not hoard cash out of habit — money sitting in your pocket is not progress here. 3) If you reach the late game short of the total, garages and high-end vehicles close it in a few purchases. 4) The purchase that crosses $100,000 pops the trophy. Tip: This pairs naturally with Little Boxes — the $160,000 of garages alone more than covers the spending total if you buy them first.
trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
trophies.source: PowerPyx trophy guide; GamesRadar+ trophy list
trophies.trigger: Spend $100,000 across any shops.

trophies.guide: Overview: Buy all 8 purchasable garages, $160,000 in total. Each garage is bought from its sale sign, so this is a savings goal, not a skill test. Steps: 1) Note garage locations as you explore, so no property is a surprise later. 2) Bank robbery income instead of spending it all on consumables. 3) Buy garages one by one as funds allow; each purchase is permanent progress. 4) The eighth garage pops the trophy. Tip: Sequence matters — garage spending also counts toward Treat Yo Self's $100,000, so buying garages early pays two trophies at once.
trophies.name: Little Boxes
trophies.source: PowerPyx trophy guide; GamesRadar+ trophy list
trophies.trigger: Buy all 8 purchasable garages ($160,000 in total).

trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Overview: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app. Any ten vehicles count, so this rewards a habit, not a hunt. Steps: 1) Open the Scooter Bros app whenever you acquire or find a vehicle worth keeping. 2) Register it on the spot rather than batching the job for later. 3) Cars you deliver for Randy's Wish List and vehicles you scan for Whip It Good are natural candidates. 4) The tenth registration pops the trophy. Tip: Players who register as they go finish this without noticing; players who postpone it face a dull ten-vehicle errand at the end.
trophies.name: On the Spot
trophies.source: PowerPyx trophy guide; GamesRadar+ trophy list
trophies.trigger: Register 10 vehicles in the Scooter Bros app.

trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Overview: Take down 5 enemies inside a single use of Combat Focus. The window is short, so the trophy is won in the preparation, not the shooting. Steps: 1) Buff your focus first — food, drinks or a shower all extend it — and carry Adrenaline. 2) Choose a clustered target: gang members at their illegal operations stand close together. 3) Position with an assault rifle loaded and all five targets in reach before you trigger Combat Focus. 4) Drop five enemies before the effect ends. Tip: If you get four, do not chase the fifth across the map — reset, re-buff and re-attempt the same cluster; the setup takes a minute and the cluster respawns.
trophies.name: Gunslinger
trophies.source: PowerPyx trophy guide; GamesRadar+ trophy list
trophies.trigger: Take down 5 enemies in one use of Combat Focus. Buff focus with food, drinks or a shower first, bring Adrenaline, use an assault rifle, and pick gang members at their illegal operations.

trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: Overview: Steal an airliner docked at a boarding bridge at VCIA and fly it at least 1 km away. Steps: 1) Enter VCIA and find an airliner docked at a boarding bridge — terminals E3 and E4 are the published spots. 2) Board it and get it moving as fast as you can; airport security responds quickly. 3) Take off and put distance between you and the airport — the requirement is 1 km. 4) Crossing that distance in the stolen airliner pops the trophy. Tip: Learn the taxi route to the runway on a harmless visit first, so the theft itself is one clean run with no wrong turns.
trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can
trophies.source: PowerPyx trophy guide; GamesRadar+ trophy list
trophies.trigger: Steal an airliner docked at a VCIA boarding bridge (terminals E3/E4 work) and fly 1 km away.

trophies.guide: Overview: Steal a Rhino tank from Mile Zero Air Station. Getting in is easy; getting the tank out under fire is the trophy. Steps: 1) Arrive armoured and armed — the base response is heavy from the first alarm. 2) Go straight for a tank rather than fighting the base; every second inside raises the pressure. 3) Drive the tank out through the exit you entered by, so no route-finding is needed under fire. 4) Once you are out with the tank, the trophy pops. Tip: A disposable fast car left at the perimeter gives you an exit if the tank is disabled — losing the tank at the gate is the common failure.
trophies.name: Challenging Tank
trophies.source: PowerPyx trophy guide; GamesRadar+ trophy list
trophies.trigger: Steal a tank at Mile Zero Air Station.

trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: Overview: The official description says only this: enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach. The trigger is unconfirmed — no reliable method has been published yet, so this guide invents none: no bar, drink or sequence is stated here as fact. Steps: 1) When you are on Ocean Beach, try the obvious reading of the description — order a cocktail somewhere with a view of the beach. 2) If it does not pop, leave it and move on; do not burn hours on an unverified method. 3) Revisit once confirmed methods are published. Tip: Honest unknown beats confident fiction — six trophies in this list, this one included, are flagged unconfirmed throughout the guide for exactly that reason.
trophies.name: In The Beginning…
trophies.source: Official PlayStation trophy list; trigger unconfirmed in published lists
trophies.trigger: Have a cocktail with an Ocean Beach view; exact trigger still unknown.

trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: Overview: The official description says only this: smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style. The trigger is unconfirmed — no reliable method has been published yet, so this guide invents none and names no specific showroom or car as the answer. Steps: 1) If you find yourself in a vehicle showroom, the description's plain reading is to drive a car out through the glass. 2) Try it once, opportunistically, when a showroom visit presents itself. 3) If it does not pop, move on rather than repeating an unverified method. Tip: Treat every unconfirmed trophy the same way — one honest attempt at the description's plain meaning, then park it until a confirmed method exists.
trophies.name: Capital Offense
trophies.source: Official PlayStation trophy list; trigger unconfirmed in published lists

trophies.guide: Overview: The official description says only this: second time's the charm. The trigger is unconfirmed — the description hints that something fails once and succeeds on a second attempt, but which thing has not been reliably identified, and this guide invents no answer. Steps: 1) Play normally and stay alert for any activity the game makes you retry. 2) If a second-attempt success feels scripted rather than accidental, note where it happened. 3) Do not grind guesses at this one — without a confirmed trigger, attempts are shots in the dark. Tip: Unconfirmed trophies often resolve themselves during a full playthrough; let this one come to you.
trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess
trophies.source: Official PlayStation trophy list; trigger unconfirmed in published lists
trophies.trigger: The description hints at a second attempt; trigger still unknown.

trophies.guide: Overview: The official description says only this: what the hell just happened? The trigger is unconfirmed — the wording hints at a strange or unexplained encounter somewhere in Leonida, but no location or event has been reliably confirmed, and this guide invents none. Steps: 1) Explore odd corners of the map when you pass them; strange encounters rarely sit on main roads. 2) Investigate anything the game presents as out of place rather than driving past it. 3) If nothing presents itself, park the trophy — it is flagged unconfirmed here precisely because guessing would mislead you. Tip: Exploration trophies like The Goodtime State raise your chances for free, since they put you in the map's strangest places anyway.

trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Overview: The official description says only this: bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by. The trigger is unconfirmed — the wording points to knocking someone down with a melee attack from a moving vehicle, but the exact conditions have not been reliably published, and this guide presents that reading as a lead, not a fact. Steps: 1) When the chance arises, try the plain reading once: a melee swing from a vehicle at a pedestrian target. 2) If it pops, the lead was right; if not, do not repeat it on a loop. 3) Revisit when a confirmed method is published. Tip: One attempt at the plain meaning is honest hunting; fifty attempts at a guess is a grind built on nothing.
trophies.name: Ten Pin
trophies.source: Official PlayStation trophy list; trigger unconfirmed in published lists

trophies.guide: Overview: Complete Gone Fishing, the opening mission of the game. It unlocks naturally in the first minutes of the story and cannot be missed. Steps: 1) Start the story and play the opening as it unfolds. 2) Follow the mission's prompts to its end. 3) The trophy pops on completion — your first of the 55. Tip: Use the opening to set two habits that pay off for 200 hours: scan everything with WAiNK, and keep a separate save at the start of the chapter.
trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.source: Official PlayStation trophy list; PowerPyx trophy guide
trophies.trigger: Finish the first story mission (Gone Fishing).

trophies.guide: Overview: Complete Chapter 1. It is story-only and cannot be missed — but Chapter 1 holds the game's one missable moment, so this chapter deserves care. Steps: 1) Play the chapter's missions in order. 2) Before the chapter closes, do the balcony meditation at Jason's house when Lucia offers it — it cannot be repeated after Chapter 1 and Positive Mental Attitude depends on it. 3) Meet Cal and Kenton while you are here; both strands open in this chapter. 4) The trophy pops at the chapter's close. Tip: Keep a save at the start and end of Chapter 1 — of all ten chapter saves the roadmap recommends, this pair is the one that insures a trophy.
trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.source: Official PlayStation trophy list; PowerPyx trophy guide
trophies.trigger: Finish Chapter 1.

trophies.guide: Overview: Complete Chapter 2. Story-only and unmissable. Steps: 1) Play the chapter's missions in order, including Breakfast Run, which carries its own trophy (Trust). 2) Visit the Thrillbilly Mudclub to open Billy's strand, which starts in this chapter. 3) Keep scanning vehicles and locations as the map widens — Chapter 2 travel is prime WAiNK territory. 4) The trophy pops at the chapter's close. Tip: Save at the chapter's start and end, as with every chapter — there is no mission replay, so saves are your only way back.
trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
trophies.source: Official PlayStation trophy list; PowerPyx trophy guide
trophies.trigger: Finish Chapter 2.

trophies.guide: Overview: Complete Chapter 3. Story-only and unmissable, and the chapter where the trophy hunt widens sharply. Steps: 1) Play the chapter's missions in order, including The Cartel Heist (Break the Bank). 2) Pick up the Snap Gun — from here, Sneakthief becomes attemptable. 3) Open the Chapter 3 strands: Andy (as Lucia), Randy's Wish List and Tyrone (as Jason). 4) The trophy pops at the chapter's close. Tip: Chapter 3 is the natural point to start the gym routine for Personal Best — both characters' Strength then builds quietly alongside the story.
trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
trophies.source: Official PlayStation trophy list; PowerPyx trophy guide
trophies.trigger: Finish Chapter 3.

trophies.guide: Overview: Complete Chapter 4. Story-only and unmissable, and the densest chapter for named-mission trophies. Steps: 1) Play the chapter's missions in order. 2) Child's Play (Family Matters), Headliners (DWNFALL) and VCIA Takedown (Hi-Jacked) each carry their own trophy inside this chapter. 3) A visit to VCIA for Hi-Jacked doubles as reconnaissance for Catch Me If You Can's airliner theft. 4) The trophy pops at the chapter's close. Tip: With the finale approaching, check your counters — stunts, scans, challenges — so the post-story cleanup list holds no surprises.
trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
trophies.source: Official PlayStation trophy list; PowerPyx trophy guide
trophies.trigger: Finish Chapter 4.

trophies.guide: Overview: Complete Breakfast Run, a Chapter 2 story mission. Story-only and unmissable — it sits directly on the campaign path. Steps: 1) Advance Chapter 2 until Breakfast Run is offered. 2) Play the mission through to completion. 3) The trophy pops as the mission closes. Tip: Named-mission trophies like this one need no preparation at all; the only mistake available is rushing past the chapter's side content, so let the strands open as you pass them.
trophies.name: Trust
trophies.source: Official PlayStation trophy list; PowerPyx trophy guide
trophies.trigger: Finish a Chapter 2 story mission (Breakfast Run).

Tip: Heist income is early seed money — bank it toward garages and laundering rather than spending it all at once, and two money trophies start moving together.
